title: 5 things to do this weekend, starting with the big ones
igCaption:
Start with the weekend plans, then watch the Saturday rain.
Oct 16 to 18, Miami and Palm Beach County, $159 to $599

Sources: The Palm Beach Post, Local 10, Miami New Times, Secret Miami

#MiamiWeekend #MiamiEvents #PalmBeachCounty #ThingsToDo

scenes.text: Want weekend plans that start in Palm Beach County and end with a thirteen-stage music festival?
Number five: No Kings protests are planned in Palm Beach County on Saturday, October 17. The Palm Beach Post says there are five protests that day.
scenes.caption: Number 5: No Kings protests are planned in Palm Beach County on Saturday, Oct. 17. The Palm Beach Post says there are 5 protests that day.

scenes.text: Number four: the Humane Society of Broward County hosts Count Bark-ula on Friday. Local 10 says adoptable puppies and big dogs are getting extra attention at the Halloween festival.
scenes.caption: Number 4: the Humane Society of Broward County hosts Count Bark-ula on Friday. Local 10 says adoptable puppies and big dogs are getting extra attention at the Halloween festival.

scenes.text: Number three: Bar1939 at the National Hotel in Miami Beach has three Halloween cocktails throughout October. One is Morticia’s Bleeding Heart Margarita, topped with lychee eyeballs, at 1677 Collins Avenue. If you’re sipping there, open NEAR and see who else is at Bar1939.

scenes.text: Number two: III Points returns to Mana Wynwood for two days. The festival starts Friday at three p.m. with thirteen stages. Miami New Times lists Flying Lotus, Tokischa, Four Tet, Lil' Kim, and Bone Thugs-n-Harmony.
scenes.caption: Number 2: III Points returns to Mana Wynwood for 2 days. The festival starts Friday at 3 p.m. with 13 stages. Miami New Times lists Flying Lotus, Tokischa, Four Tet, Lil' Kim, and Bone Thugs-n-Harmony.

scenes.text: Number one: plan around Saturday rain. Local 10 says widespread thunderstorms start around one to three p.m. Saturday. Some rain could be heavy and lead to flooding, with high rain chances lasting into Saturday night.

scenes.text: Which one would you actually do this weekend? A weekend in South Florida is full of people you notice and never meet, and NEAR is for the ones you passed by without ever learning who they were.
